steps.content: █/14, 2:41 AM, Chief's Office.
You flip through the files Dr. Das had handed over, back in the office.
This looks like a regular Eastside medical chart, but the details here... they're anything but ordinary diagnosis and treatment.

Name: Donald   Gender: Male   Age: █
Medical Record Number: █████████
Diagnosis: Donald, a Sinner from West District and the leader of the notorious "Rustfire" terror faction, was heavily tainted by Mania during the BR-002 event. Marked by Hush for survival, he narrowly escaped death.
From N.F. 104 to N.F. 105, he was repeatedly manipulated and tasked with handling Rustfire operations, causing IV mental trauma. Resistant yet unadaptable, he failed to undergo the puppet conversion, leading to his transfer to our institution for advanced treatment.
Currently, Donald is grappling with intense schizophrenia, has lost all speech, and shows no reaction to the outside world. As a high-value S-Class Sinner, he's a prime candidate for advanced experimental research. Following top-level directives, he's been moved to Lab B4 for continued study and intervention.
As you keep turning the pages, what comes next is even more shockingly eye-opening.

Medical Log:
On █/█/106, initiated participation in the power augmentation trials for the Sinners.
On █/█/106, attempted external stimulation through electrocution, acid exposure, extreme heat, and cryogenic methods. The subject nearly died three times without any notable rise in the M-value.

On █/█/107, the patient showed subdued brain activity, failing to produce vital emotional reactions. The only notable spike in mental activity was observed during what appeared to be dreams about the BR-002 incident. These spikes are detrimental to the patient. While this has left him unable to resist for an extended time, it has also severely hindered the project's timeline.

As of █/█/107, the patient will be transferred to psychiatric care bi-weekly. This decision by Lab B4 aims to partially rehabilitate the patient's mental health, anticipating improved outcomes in future experiments.

As of █/█/108, Lab B4 has concluded that the patient no longer holds research value. The request for his benign processing was overruled by senior management. Considering the patient's inability to function independently, permission was granted to step up psychiatric interventions. Nonetheless, constant supervision by an assigned officer is mandatory. In case of any irregularities, both the patient and any related staff will be subject to benign processing.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Why are you still up so late?
Donald wears a smile, but his hands are far from idle. He nonchalantly flings the document onto the topmost shelf of the office bookcase.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: There's no use reading that.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: These medical records, crammed with bureaucratic speak, won't really tell you what's happening at the Fourth Hospital. If it's the truth you're after, better to come see me directly.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Oh, worried you'll hurt my fragile emotions?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: It's fine. I have always had a knack for moving on. It's been ages, hasn't it...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Alright, quick now, we've got to head back to Eastside at dawn. Any burning questions? Ask away.
Donald pulls up a chair and positions himself in front of you.
He looks completely at ease, almost as if he has genuinely moved on from the past events.
After a brief moment of thought, you voice your first question.

options: What's the real deal with Banyan Fourth Hospital?

choices.text: What's the real deal with Banyan Fourth Hospital?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: It's part of Nirvana.
Donald answers, cutting to the chase.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: The mental hospital? It's just a smokescreen. On the surface, the Fourth Hospital seems to be a part of the Banyan system, but in truth, Nirvana pulls all the strings.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: What they really do there is run human experiments and secretly take care of the dirty work—those "issues" Nirvana can't sort out in the daylight.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Folks like Das? They're just part of the show, handling what they claim to be their "core business"—it's all for show for the people of Eastside.
You know, you kept some cards close to your chest during our last chat.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Well...
Donald scratches his head, appearing slightly embarrassed.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: I was worried you might let your justice radar go off the charts. What if, in a moment of rage, you end up leading a charge into the Fourth Hospital, taking everyone out?
Do you really think of me like that?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Hey, I'm just messing with you. Look, I'm mainly here to ask for your help. It wouldn't be cool to keep pitting you against others, right?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Totally my fault! From now on, I'll spill the beans immediately on anything that comes up, no more hiding!
...Alright. Moving on.
What's been your journey like since then?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: What happens next after going through that?
I just saw that the B4 Lab has labeled you "no longer holds research value"...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Ah, that bit.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: I was still locked up in the lab's infirmary afterward, though they hardly took me for experiments anymore. Guess they really got bored of me, huh?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Dr. Das would drop by now and then, giving me meds and doing some physiotherapy.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Then... the game changer happened.
Donald cracks a secretive grin, leaning in a bit.
The game changer?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: You bet! It was Samuel.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Guess what? An old-timer from the West District, posing as a cleaner, managed to infiltrate Nirvana's turf solo... and, incredibly, he located me.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Then, we teamed up, united in purpose, delivering the final blow... Though, really, it was his hustle, back and forth, that leaked the info and kicked up a whole lot of fuss.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Oh yeah, and there was that self-proclaimed poet lady. Don't know how, but she ended up at the Fourth Hospital and, believe it or not, she waltzed past the guards and slipped into the underground facility.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: She filled me in on Julien building Drifter Camp, and even said Rustfire is back in action. Man, was I thrilled to hear all that—it was like a spark lit up in my brain...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Can you believe it? The sickness just vanished right then and there, and never came back. It's no wonder they say "good news beats the best medicine"...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: But I'm not knocking Dr. Das' skills. Without his care and his round-the-clock guard against the Fourth Hospital's endless "experiments," I probably wouldn't have made it.
As Donald shares his story, his smile never wavers, remaining ever-present.
It's tough to picture his nightmare of an experience, and yet when he talks about it now, it sounds as carefree as discussing the weather.
But, reality might not be as laid-back as he lets on.
So, you really started to heal mentally, way after Samuel rescued you, huh?
Seeing Donald's face twist into what looks like a grimace of discomfort, you press on:
Back then, even after he stumbled upon you, he couldn't talk to you. You "had lost all speech, and showed no reaction to the outside world."
And Dr. Das couldn't shield you anymore, especially now when he's barely hanging on himself.
So, those days of being locked up and tormented went on till N.F. 112, didn't they?
As you fire question after question, a hint of resignation creeps into Donald's smile.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: You know, I figure... it's not really important to split hairs over it.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: The hardest times are over, and I've moved on. Why get bogged down counting every bit of pain I've been through?
In that moment, as Donald utters those words, his face radiates pure sincerity, free from any shadow of doubt in his eyes and brows.
It hits you all at once—maybe you've been too obsessed with "revealing the truth."
Sorry...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Hey, hey, hey, no need to say sorry, it's all good... Eesh, cut the formal act, you're making my skin crawl with these goosebumps.
Donald keeps waving his hands off. Confronted with your sincere apology, he oddly appears rather uneasy.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Back to the main point, huh? Got more questions? Fire away, ha...
Donald lets out an exaggerated yawn.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Seriously, it's this late and you're not sleepy? I'm beat.
You think for a second and then come up with another question.
Why did you have Raven go back to Drifter Camp and spread the news of your "death"?
Donald straightens up, an air of secrecy about him, and responds:

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: How about this—if I say I instantly knew that "great poet" was all talk, no show, would you buy it?
...Yeah, I'd buy it.
You lock eyes for a moment, and after a brief silence, you both start laughing out loud.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Hahahaha...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: This is the first time I've realized how thrilling it is to talk smack about someone behind their back, hahaha...
While chuckling, Donald continues to explain:

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Back then, I figured, this lady was a real yarn-spinner; gaining trust in Drifter Camp wouldn't be easy for her. If she started saying I was alive, she'd likely be shown the door right away.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: But you know her, she's decent at heart and as a Sinner, if she got into Drifter Camp, she could really make a difference.
Is that why you cooked up this whole story for her?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: She did most of the work; I just added a few touches. But who knew it would go so well—the "great poet" got in without a hitch, calmed things down at Drifter Camp, and really stepped up later...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: In hindsight, that strategy was spot on. If the "great poet" had spread the word about me being alive and let Drifter Camp know I was in Nirvana's clutches...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Better they're skeptical. If they actually bought it and stormed Nirvana's stronghold, it'd be a suicide mission. That would've been a real disaster.
You nod thoughtfully and go on to ask:
Once you were back on your feet, teaming up with Samuel on the outside...
Given your skills, did the idea of escaping ever cross your mind?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Naturally, it did.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Back then, I was marked by a Hush. And the odds of not getting snagged again after my escape were pretty slim...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: But what really keeps me up at night are the folks I left behind at the Fourth Hospital.
You think Nirvana might go after Das and the crew in revenge?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: And it's not just a chance, it's a guarantee they'll strike back.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Letting Das treat me was only so I'd be of some use in their experiments. If I got fully healed and slipped away, Das would be in deep water, no doubt about it.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Das has always been butting heads with them, plus he's got a lot of dirt he shouldn't... With Nirvana's no-holds-barred tactics, it's a toss-up if he'll make it out alive.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: That's why I chose to stick around a bit longer.
Donald is all smug.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Turned out to be a classic case of "not seeing what's right under your nose." Those folks at the Fourth Hospital never caught on that I was just playing crazy, hahaha.
You mean to tell me you played the madman till N.F. 112 and never got busted? That's incredible!

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Well, how else would I bag the title of a top-notch actor... Obviously, a lot of it was down to Samuel and Das playing along.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Get this, I once faked my own death. Boy, did I nail it. Those Fourth Hospital guys actually carted me off to the crematorium...
So, what happened next?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: What else was there to do? Played the zombie.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Gave those jerks the fright of their lives; ended up in the hole for a month.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Post that, escaping wasn't high on my to-do list.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Ah, it's not like I didn't try, I just couldn't find a way out...
So, how did you manage to break free in the end?
Donald gestures with open hands.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Frankly, I'm not too sure.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Suddenly, one day, I got this order from Paradeisos and next thing I know, I was being hauled off to the Executive Committee.
Any idea who signed off on that order?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: It's Hush X's signature on the Transfer Order, but who knows if she's the one behind it.
You're not worried about a hidden plot?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Why worry? There's nothing to fear.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Doesn't matter if it was X or someone else, the bottom line is they got me out, right?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Looks like that Paradeisian is probably in our corner, aiming to throw a wrench in Nirvana's plans.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: If Paradeisos's really in lockstep with Nirvana, singing the same tune, then we're really out of luck.
You nod in agreement. Interestingly, Donald's view echoes what you've always believed.
As you ride that thought, you suddenly have an epiphany, a smirk naturally forming on your face.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: What are you thinking about? What's with that sudden devilish smirk?
Donald gazes at your face, clearly baffled.
I'm thinking... if Paradeisos isn't all on the same page, then maybe, if I blow the lid off some things, the higher-ups won't necessarily rush to their rescue, huh?

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Whoa! Planning to rat people out, huh?
Yep, that's right. I'm gonna spill the beans.
Eastside is at a crossroads with public sentiment shifting. A bunch of politicians are on standby to declare their stance.
Imagine the fallout if we dig up the past squabbles between the Fourth Hospital and Nirvana now. You know what's gonna happen, right?
Or, we might just decide... to keep it under wraps.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: You mean...
Right, exactly what's on your mind.
Some cards are more intimidating in hand than on the table...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: That's a clever strategy... It neither tips them off nor backs them into a corner. It also lets us play hardball.
Donald gives his leg a hearty slap and jumps up.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Okay, that's the plan!

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: I'll get in touch with some old pals, and cook up something big for the Fourth Hospital...
Seeing the fire in Donald's eyes, you can't help but gesture towards the clock.
...Maybe take a look at the time?
It's pretty late. You sure your friends will still be up for a chat?
Donald gives a lighthearted laugh, ruffling his hair.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: True, true, time to hit the hay.
He turns and stretches out, yawning widely.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Better get some sleep yourself, you know. All these late nights could take a toll on you.
Appreciate your worry, Mr. Donald. Though, I've caught up on plenty of sleep not long ago...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Haha, you've got a point there.
